chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

I said, “May Allah keep you well! We gather together and discuss what is with us. Nothing is brought to us except that we have something written regarding it, and that is from what Allah has bestowed upon us through you. Then a small matter comes to us for which we have nothing, so some of us look to others, while we have something resembling it, and we make analogy according to what seems best of it.”
So he said, “What have you to do with analogy? Those before you were only destroyed by analogy.”
Then he said, “When there comes to you that which you know, then speak by it; and if there comes to you that which you do not know, then—” and he gestured with his hand toward his mouth.
Then he said, “May Allah curse Abū Ḥanīfah. He used to say: ‘ʿAlī said, and I say; and the Companions said, and I say.’”

Then he said, “Did you use to sit with him?” I said, “No, but this is his speech.” Then I said, “May Allah keep you well! Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bring the people what would suffice them in his time?” He said, “Yes, and what they would need until the Day of Judgment.” I said, “So has anything of that been lost?” He said, “No, it is with its أهل.”

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: its rightful possessors, namely those entrusted with this knowledge
key_terms.الصَّحَابَةُ: the Companions, mentioned here in reported speech
key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: analogy used as an independent method of deriving rulings
key_terms.مَا تَعْلَمُونَ: that which is known with certainty from transmitted guidance
key_terms.مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ: that which is not known and should not be spoken about without knowledge
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, marking the enduring sufficiency of revealed guidance

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about qiyās and the source of religious knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith forbids resorting to qiyās when no explicit teaching is known, and instructs believers to speak only on what they know from the transmitted guidance. It also affirms that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله conveyed all that the community would need until the Day of Judgment, and that this knowledge remains with its rightful أهل.
